clue.text: Take risk and get dismissed leg before?

definitions.meaning: to put yourself in a precarious position, out where support is thin
read literally, to be given out in cricket with the leg (a limb) in front of the wicket, the dismissal called LBW

explanation.surface: A batsman gambles on a shot and is given out leg before wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batter is 'out leg before wicket' (LBW) when the ball strikes the leg in front of the stumps; the second reading treats that as being out on a leg, a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to take a chance by adopting an exposed position, like climbing out along a branch.

clue.text: Left amid rocky earth with bent tent pegs, don't give up!

indicators.note: amid means the letter for left sits within the shuffled letters
rocky means unsteady, so the letters of earth are jumbled
bent means twisted out of shape, so the letters of tent pegs are jumbled too

explanation.surface: A camper struggling with bent pegs in stony ground is urged to persevere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent' jumbles TENT PEGS and 'rocky' jumbles those together with EARTH; 'amid' puts L inside the result, just before the final E. 'rocky earth' reads as stony ground, hiding the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to tackle a difficulty boldly, so it works as an exhortation to keep going rather than shrink back.

clue.text: Took a picture, capturing exotic creature

indicators.note: capturing means the words took a picture hold the letters within them

explanation.surface: A wildlife photographer snapped a shot of an unusual animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across tOOK A PIcture.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a rare striped forest mammal of central Africa, a relative of the giraffe, so it is an unusual beast.

clue.text: Polluted lake I abandoned

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain lake
shed means cast off or abandoned

explanation.surface: A lake has become polluted and I have left it behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tarnished is stained or sullied, which is what pollution does to it.

clue.text: It's impossible to pinch two kilos from Speyside distillery

indicators.note: to pinch means to steal, so these letters are taken away from the distillery name

parts.note: Knockando is a whisky distillery in Speyside, a malt-whisky region of Scotland
K is the abbreviation for kilo, so two kilos give two Ks

explanation.surface: Someone is told they can't steal two kilos of whisky from a Scottish distillery.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove both Ks from KNOCKANDO; 'from' just links the theft to its source.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang reply is a flat refusal meaning the thing cannot be done.

clue.text: Chance on American plant

parts.note: a lot is a chance or fortune, as in drawing lots
US stands for the United States, so American

explanation.surface: A US plant was stumbled on by chance.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a water lily, an aquatic flowering species.

clue.text: Delivery heard from His Master's Voice?

indicators.note: heard tells us the phrase is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same but is spelt differently

parts.note: a man's voice giving a command is a male order

explanation.surface: Something delivered as heard from the HMV record label, whose dog listens to a gramophone.
explanation.walkthrough: His Master's Voice (HMV) is a famous British record label; read literally, it is a man issuing a command.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods bought by post arrive by delivery, so the postal shopping system is defined by how it reaches you.

clue.text: What bean-counter might do to offer life assurance?

definitions.meaning: pulses are beans and lentils, so someone counting beans checks pulses
taking someone's pulse reassures them that they are alive

explanation.surface: An accountant might double as an insurance salesman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bean-counter' is slang for an accountant and 'life assurance' is insurance, but both are read literally: counting pulses and assuring life.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling the beat at your wrist both counts the legumes in the pun and proves you are alive.

clue.text: Extreme characters one found in pub and market

indicators.note: found in means these letters sit inside the pub word

parts.note: a bar is a pub
A and Z are the alphabet's extreme letters
A means one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: Odd characters gather in a pub and a market.
explanation.definitionFit: A bazaar is an eastern marketplace or a fundraising sale.

clue.text: Spooner's big bird in vicious encounter

indicators.note: Spooner's signals swapping the opening sounds of two words

parts.note: fat means big
a kite is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: A large bird is in a savage fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of FAT KITE gives the phrase, with the K sound spelt C.
explanation.definitionFit: A brawl with scratching and hair-pulling is a fierce, nasty clash.

clue.text: Point out spies infiltrating supplier of observation equipment

indicators.note: infiltrating means the spies get inside the jumbled letters
out means disordered, so the letters of point are rearranged

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency

explanation.surface: Someone notes that spies have infiltrated a firm making surveillance gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point out' looks like one verb meaning indicate, but 'out' is the anagram signal, making OPTIN; 'infiltrating' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional who dispenses spectacles provides the equipment that helps people see, cheekily called observation gear.

clue.text: Pet animal noise disturbing school

indicators.note: disturbing means the noise breaks into the school letters

parts.note: moo is the noise of a cow

explanation.surface: A pet's noise disrupts lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: To pet is to kiss and cuddle, a synonym for the verb.

clue.text: Without whom lunch effectively impossible?

indicators.note: the words lunch effectively hold the letters inside them, from the outside in

explanation.surface: No midday meal could happen without one particular person.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit in lunCH EFfectively, while the whole clue describes the cook.
explanation.definitionFit: The cook in a restaurant kitchen makes the meal, so without that person there would be no lunch.

clue.text: Head off the company south of Sherwood?

indicators.note: south of means below, so in a down entry the company letters come after

parts.note: Sherwood is a forest in Nottinghamshire, Robin Hood's home
all means everyone present, the whole company

explanation.surface: Robin Hood's band head off south from Sherwood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' looks like leaving; it means prevent.
explanation.definitionFit: To head someone off is to prevent them by acting first, a synonym for pre-empting.

clue.text: Pirate might have one each of these with which to make fast

definitions.text: Pirate might have one each of these
definitions.meaning: a storybook pirate has a hook for a hand and one good eye beside an eyepatch
a fastener for clothing, a small metal hook catching a loop

explanation.surface: A pirate's equipment for securing something.
explanation.definitionFit: The fastener is a small hook clipping into a loop on garments, and a pirate cartoon has a hook hand and a single eye.

clue.text: Consequences of when Washington recess may be timetabled?

definitions.meaning: results or repercussions that follow an event

definitions.text: when Washington recess may be timetabled?
definitions.meaning: Americans say math for maths, and a school recess might come after that lesson

explanation.surface: Political fallout when Congress breaks for a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Washington recess' suggests Congress, but here it is an American school break, scheduled after math class.
explanation.definitionFit: The period following a disaster brings its results, so the word means repercussions.

clue.text: Get dinner prepared with one? At least!

definitions.text: Get dinner prepared with one? At least!

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so the letters of get dinner are reworked

explanation.surface: A cook asks if they can make dinner with only one item, and is told that's the minimum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges GET DINNER, and 'with' adds I alongside.
explanation.definitionFit: A component of a recipe; any dish needs at least one item going into it.

clue.text: Improve hen gathering with topless disco

indicators.note: gathering means the letters of hen are pulled together into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a disco is a dance

explanation.surface: A hen party is livened up by a disco where clothing is optional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hen gathering' suggests a hen party, but 'gathering' rearranges HEN into ENH; 'topless' strips D from DANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To enhance something is to make it better, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Regret saying something saucy

indicators.note: saying means spoken aloud, giving a different spelling of the same sound

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Someone is sorry for a rude remark.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooked mix of butter and flour that thickens sauces, the base of a béchamel.

clue.text: Street unchanged — because of this?

parts.note: as is means in its current state, unchanged

explanation.surface: A street remains the same, and someone wonders why.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a state of inactivity, where nothing changes, which explains an unaltered street.

clue.text: Spare eggs served up on end of toast

indicators.note: served up means brought upward, so in a down entry the eggs word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: nits are the eggs of lice

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of toast

explanation.surface: Breakfast: leftover eggs on toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spare' looks like an adjective (leftover) but is the verb, to give sparingly. Nits are lice eggs; 'served up' turns them upward in this down entry, and 'end of' picks a final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To be sparing is to be frugal, and the verb means to supply grudgingly.

clue.text: Measure high-quality car taking bend at speed with throaty noise

parts.note: HA is the abbreviation for hectare, a measure of area
RR stands for Rolls-Royce, a luxury car
a U-bend is a bend in a pipe
mph, miles per hour, is a measure of speed

explanation.surface: A luxury car takes a corner at speed with a throaty engine noise.
explanation.definitionFit: The sound is a gruff clearing of the throat that conveys disapproval.

clue.text: Superior meal has no starter

indicators.note: has no starter means the first letter is dropped, punning on a meal's first course

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: A posh dinner skips the first course.
explanation.definitionFit: Higher in rank or position, so the word works as a synonym for superior.

clue.text: Dog did as told, perhaps, separating men

indicators.note: separating means the action word sits between the two names

parts.note: Al and Ian are two men's names
sat is what an obedient dog does when told

explanation.surface: An obedient dog stands between two men.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed is a German shepherd dog, a large working breed.

clue.text: To hit old man back is shocking

indicators.note: back means the hit and old man words are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to slap is to hit
pa means father, informally one's old man

explanation.surface: Hitting your father back would be scandalous.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means horrifies or dismays, the effect of something shocking.

clue.text: Model reluctant to enter church on Sunday in front of Rector wearing stockings

indicators.note: to enter means the reluctant word goes inside the church letters

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England
loth means unwilling

indicators.note: wearing means the rector letter is clothed by the stockings word

parts.note: hose means stockings or tights

explanation.surface: A model is unwilling to attend church on Sunday ahead of the rector in stockings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' is a disparaging term for a fashion-conscious person; 'on' and 'in front of' just order the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal term for someone who loves wearing fashionable garments, like a mannequin.
